facts.fact: 叙述者最熟悉的闹鬼之地是 Luton 酒店——旧酒店的躯壳像被抛弃的恋人一样倾颓。
facts.anchor: Of the haunted places, the one I know best is the Luton Hotel.

facts.fact: Uncle Redbird 抱怨酒店「给好色者的房间比给病人还多」：医院只有二十张床，酒店却有三十五间房。
facts.anchor: “More rooms for the lecherous than for the sickly,” Uncle Redbird would grumble.

facts.fact: 酒店的地基是用偷来的「祖父石」建的——Redbird 称之为「奴隶石」。
facts.anchor: because of asiniig, the rocks. Three stories high, the hotel’s white clapboard torso sat on a stone and mortar foundation. Slave rocks, Redbird called them.

facts.fact: 传闻酒店老板雇流浪汉采石，五个人开工，发薪日只剩三个。
facts.anchor: Rumor is the hotel owners hired hobos to harvest the stones. Five men started the job, only three remained on payday.

facts.fact: 石头离开故土后开始哭泣，造成的积水被归咎于排水不良。
facts.anchor: Away from their natural home, the rocks wept.

facts.fact: 最终祖父石烧毁了酒店——许多人认为是 Redbird 或叙述者干的，因为他们互为不在场证明。
facts.anchor: THE GRANDFATHERS BURNED the building finally.

facts.fact: 结尾：叙述者记得石头如兄弟，用长满老茧的手指数着每一次被移走。
facts.anchor: But I remember stone—as a brother. On my calloused fingers I count all of the removals.
